title: Structure of the Periodic Table
content:
# Structure of the Periodic Table

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Describe the structure of the periodic table
- Identify groups, periods, and blocks
- Locate metals, non-metals, and metalloids
- Explain how position relates to properties

## Introduction

The **periodic table** is organised in a specific way that reflects the structure of atoms. Understanding its layout helps predict the properties and behaviour of elements.

## Key Concepts

### Basic Layout

[DIAGRAM: Periodic table showing groups 1-8/0, periods 1-7, s-block, p-block, d-block labelled, metals and non-metals areas shaded differently]

**The periodic table is arranged in:**
- **Rows** = Periods (numbered 1-7)
- **Columns** = Groups (numbered 1-7, then 0 or 1-18)

### Groups (Vertical Columns)

**Group:** A vertical column of elements with similar properties.

| Group | Name | Number of outer electrons |
|-------|------|---------------------------|
| 1 | Alkali metals | 1 |
| 2 | Alkaline earth metals | 2 |
| 3-12 | Transition metals | Variable |
| 7 (17) | Halogens | 7 |
| 0 (18) | Noble gases | 8 (or 2 for helium) |

**Elements in the same group have:**
- Same number of electrons in outer shell
- Similar chemical properties
- Similar reactions

**Note:** Two numbering systems exist:
- Traditional: 1, 2, then transition metals, then 3-7, 0
- IUPAC: 1-18 across

### Periods (Horizontal Rows)

**Period:** A horizontal row of elements.

| Period | Elements | Electron shells filled |
|--------|----------|-----------------------|
| 1 | H, He | 1st shell (up to 2) |
| 2 | Li to Ne | 2nd shell (up to 8) |
| 3 | Na to Ar | 3rd shell (up to 8) |
| 4 | K to Kr | 3rd shell (8-18), 4th shell |

**Elements in the same period have:**
- Same number of electron shells
- Properties that change across the period
- Transition from metals to non-metals (left to right)

### Blocks

The periodic table is divided into blocks based on which orbital is being filled:

| Block | Groups | Orbital being filled |
|-------|--------|---------------------|
| s-block | 1-2 | s orbitals |
| p-block | 13-18 (3-0) | p orbitals |
| d-block | 3-12 | d orbitals (transition metals) |
| f-block | Lanthanides/Actinides | f orbitals |

### Metals, Non-metals, and Metalloids

[DIAGRAM: Periodic table with metals on left (shaded), non-metals on right, metalloid staircase in between]

**Metals:**
- Left and centre of the table
- About 80% of elements
- Shiny, conduct electricity, malleable, ductile
- Form positive ions (lose electrons)

**Non-metals:**
- Right side of the table
- Dull, poor conductors (mostly), brittle
- Form negative ions (gain electrons) or covalent bonds

**Metalloids (Semi-metals):**
- Along the "staircase" dividing metals and non-metals
- B, Si, Ge, As, Sb, Te, Po
- Have properties of both metals and non-metals
- Often semiconductors

### Key Groups to Know

| Group | Position | Key elements | Properties |
|-------|----------|--------------|------------|
| Group 1 | Far left | Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs | Very reactive metals |
| Group 2 | Second column | Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba | Reactive metals |
| Group 7 | Second from right | F, Cl, Br, I | Reactive non-metals |
| Group 0 | Far right | He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe | Unreactive gases |
| Transition metals | Centre | Fe, Cu, Zn, etc. | Less reactive metals |

### Trends in the Periodic Table

**Across a period (left to right):**
- Metallic character decreases
- Atomic radius decreases
- Elements change from metals to non-metals

**Down a group:**
- Metallic character increases (for Groups 1-2)
- Atomic radius increases
- Reactivity changes (increases for metals, decreases for halogens)

## Worked Examples

**Example 1:** An element is in Group 2 and Period 3. Identify the element and describe its properties.

**Solution:**
- Group 2, Period 3 = **Magnesium (Mg)**
- Properties:
  - Metal (left side of table)
  - 2 electrons in outer shell (Group 2)
  - 3 electron shells (Period 3)
  - Will form Mg²⁺ ions (loses 2 electrons)
  - Moderately reactive metal

---

**Example 2:** Explain why elements in the same group have similar chemical properties.

**Solution:**
- Elements in the same group have the same number of electrons in their outer shell
- Chemical reactions involve outer shell electrons
- Same number of outer electrons = similar ways of reacting
- For example, all Group 1 elements have 1 outer electron
- They all lose this electron easily to form +1 ions
- This gives them similar chemical properties

---

**Example 3:** Silicon is often described as a metalloid. Explain why.

**Solution:**
- Silicon is located on the "staircase" between metals and non-metals
- It has some metallic properties:
  - Shiny appearance
  - Can conduct electricity (when heated or doped)
- It has some non-metallic properties:
  - Brittle (not malleable)
  - Forms covalent bonds
- Its intermediate properties make it a metalloid
- It's used as a semiconductor in electronics

## Common Mistakes

- **Mistake:** Thinking Group 0 elements have 0 electrons
- **Correct:** Group 0 (noble gases) have FULL outer shells (8, or 2 for He)

- **Mistake:** Confusing groups and periods
- **Correct:** Groups are vertical (similar properties); Periods are horizontal (same shells)

- **Mistake:** Thinking all elements on the left are non-metals
- **Correct:** Metals are on the LEFT; non-metals on the RIGHT

## Practice Questions

1. Define the terms 'group' and 'period' in the periodic table. (2 marks)

2. An element has 17 protons. State its group number and period number. (2 marks)

3. Explain why elements in the same period have the same number of electron shells. (2 marks)

4. Describe how the properties of elements change across Period 3 from sodium to argon. (4 marks)

5. Explain the difference between metals and non-metals in terms of their:
   a) Position in the periodic table (1 mark)
   b) Electron behaviour when forming ions (2 marks)

6. What is a metalloid? Give two examples and explain why they are classified this way. (4 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Group | A vertical column in the periodic table |
| Period | A horizontal row in the periodic table |
| Block | A section of the table based on electron orbitals (s, p, d, f) |
| Metalloid | An element with properties between metals and non-metals |
| Transition metal | A metal in the d-block of the periodic table |

## Summary

- **Groups:** Vertical columns - same outer electrons, similar properties
- **Periods:** Horizontal rows - same number of electron shells
- **Metals:** Left and centre - lose electrons, form positive ions
- **Non-metals:** Right side - gain electrons or share, form negative ions or covalent bonds
- **Metalloids:** Along the staircase - intermediate properties
- **Key groups:** 1 (alkali metals), 2 (alkaline earth), 7 (halogens), 0 (noble gases)
- **Across a period:** Metal → metalloid → non-metal → noble gas
